NUMBER 7 OF 2024

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and innate characteristics without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, and environments located in the industrial sector.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic designation that can be used by various institutions providing services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. which specifically have the principal duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts for the protection of women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and residing in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 21. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent to a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, suffering or distress either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Recovery of Victims is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25. Integrated Service is the provision of integrated services, multi-aspects, cross-function and sector for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders suffered. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is a technical operational implementation unit within the work unit that carries out government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, exploitation, discrimination, and other problems. 33. Temporary Shelter is a service function to provide or provide access to temporary protection places that prioritize security and safety, as well as clothing, food, and supporting facilities for beneficiary needs. 34. Standard Operating Procedures, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.

Article 24

In the effort to protect women victims of violence, the Regional Government shall be obligated to:

a. ensure the implementation of the fulfillment of women's rights and the provision of guarantees of security from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the region;
b. establish policies, programs, women's protection activities and guarantees for victim handling to eliminate all forms of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the region; and
c. provide guidance and supervision in the efforts to protect women carried out by the Regional Apparatus that handles governmental affairs in the field of Protection and Empowerment of Women.

Article 2

Letter a What is meant by respect for human rights is respect for, upholding human rights inherent in citizens, as well as protecting dignity and honor as human beings.

Letter b What is meant by non-discrimination is protection for all women without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, belief, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, political choice, legal status and physical or mental condition. Special treatment or action toward vulnerable groups of women with the aim that they obtain equality of rights is not included as an act of discrimination.

Letter c What is meant by gender justice is fair treatment given to women and men. What is meant by gender equality is a condition and position that describes equal, harmonious and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d What is meant by benefit is the implementation of women's protection that provides benefits to women in the form of welfare, equality and justice, security and avoidance of all forms of violence, exploitation and discrimination.

Article 13

(1) The implementation of Women Empowerment in the field of health as referred to in Article 12 paragraph (2) letter a shall be carried out by Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of health.

(2) The form of empowerment in the field of health as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of reproductive and sexual health services that are healthy, safe, and free from coercion and/or violence.

(3) Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) include:

a. health services for the period before pregnancy, pregnancy, childbirth and after childbirth;
b. pregnancy regulation, contraceptive services and sexual health;
c. reproductive health services; and
d. services and provision of adequate lactation rooms in every Regional government agency, public facilities and industry.
(4) Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out through promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative approaches.

Article 14

(1) Women Empowerment in the field of education as referred to in Article 12 paragraph (2) letter b shall be carried out by Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of education in the form of organizing formal and non-formal education.

(2) Non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to improve the capabilities of women.

(3) Non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (2) includes the provision of skills and job training.

CHAPTER II

RIGHTS OF WOMEN

Article 27

(1) In order to coordinate and synchronize policies, programs and women's protection activities to eliminate all acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the Region, the Mayor shall establish a task force, forum, working group or other institutions.

(2) The membership of the task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of relevant Regional Apparatus, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.

(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment of the task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in the Mayor Regulation.

Article 32

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women shall be conducted by the Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of Women Empowerment and Child Protection periodically.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the following year.

Article 34

Further provisions regarding monitoring, evaluation, and reporting of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women as referred to in Article 31 through Article 33 shall be regulated in the Mayor Regulation.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and innate characteristics without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, and environments located in the industrial sector.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic designation that can be used by various institutions providing services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. which specifically have the principal duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts for the protection of women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Surakarta City. 2. Mayor is the Mayor of Surakarta. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Apparatus is the supporting element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region; 5. Woman is a person who is female from infancy, adolescence, adulthood to the elderly, who is recognized by law. 6. Protection is all efforts to fulfill rights and provide assistance to provide a sense of security to witnesses and/or victims that must be carried out by institutions in accordance with legislation. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties aimed at protecting women from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination as well as providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights. 8. Empowerment of Women is an effort to gain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept and be free from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion, directly or indirectly, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, both individual and collective, in the fields of politics, economics, law, education, social, culture and other aspects of life. 10. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ exploitation, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to gain both material and immaterial benefits. 11. Violence is any act that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstruction of the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 12. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually and psychologically including certain acts of arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 13. Online Gender-Based Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as KBGO, is violence that occurs through digital media or online platforms targeting women, including: comments or messages that are insulting, degrading, or belittling of Women, messages or comments threatening to commit physical or sexual violence against Women, disseminating victims' personal information (such as addresses, telephone numbers, or other identities) without permission with the aim of intimidating or harming victims, extortion involving threats to spread intimate images or videos of victims unless the victim meets the perpetrator's demands, spreading private photos or videos of an intimate nature without the consent of the woman in the content, use of technology to stalk or monitor victims continuously, often with the aim of frightening or controlling the victim, and digitally altering images or videos of women for the purpose of insulting, humiliating, or sexually exploiting. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, contraceptive coercion, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of human trafficking aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly referred to as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of legislation. 18.

Article 24

In the effort to protect women victims of violence, the Regional Government shall be obligated to:

a. ensure the implementation of the fulfillment of women's rights and the provision of guarantees of security from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the region;
b. establish policies, programs, women's protection activities and guarantees for victim handling to eliminate all forms of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the region; and
c. provide guidance and supervision in the efforts to protect women carried out by the Regional Apparatus that handles governmental affairs in the field of Protection and Empowerment of Women.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and innate characteristics without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, and environments located in the industrial sector.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic designation that can be used by various institutions providing services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. which specifically have the principal duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts for the protection of women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 27

(1) In order to coordinate and synchronize policies, programs and women's protection activities to eliminate all acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the Region, the Mayor shall establish a task force, forum, working group or other institutions.

(2) The membership of the task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of relevant Regional Apparatus, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.

(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment of the task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in the Mayor Regulation.

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and residing in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 21. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent to a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, suffering or distress either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Recovery of Victims is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25. Integrated Service is the provision of integrated services, multi-aspects, cross-function and sector for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders suffered. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is a technical operational implementation unit within the work unit that carries out government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, exploitation, discrimination, and other problems. 33. Temporary Shelter is a service function to provide or provide access to temporary protection places that prioritize security and safety, as well as clothing, food, and supporting facilities for beneficiary needs. 34. Standard Operating Procedures, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.

Article 1

Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Woman is a person who is female from infancy, adolescence, adulthood to the elderly, who is recognized by law. 6. Protection is all efforts to fulfill rights and provide assistance to provide a sense of security to witnesses and/or victims that must be carried out by institutions in accordance with legislation. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties aimed at protecting women from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination as well as providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights. 8. Empowerment of Women is an effort to gain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept and be free from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion, directly or indirectly, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, both individual and collective, in the fields of politics, economics, law, education, social, culture and other aspects of life. 10. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ exploitation, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to gain both material and immaterial benefits. 11. Violence is any act that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstruction of the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 12. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually and psychologically including certain acts of arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 13. Online Gender-Based Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as KBGO, is violence that occurs through digital media or online platforms targeting women, including: comments or messages that are insulting, degrading, or belittling of Women, messages or comments threatening to commit physical or sexual violence against Women, disseminating victims' personal information (such as addresses, telephone numbers, or other identities) without permission with the aim of intimidating or harming victims, extortion involving threats to spread intimate images or videos of victims unless the victim meets the perpetrator's demands, spreading private photos or videos of an intimate nature without the consent of the woman in the content, use of technology to stalk or monitor victims continuously, often with the aim of frightening or controlling the victim, and digitally altering images or videos of women for the purpose of insulting, humiliating, or sexually exploiting. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, contraceptive coercion, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of human trafficking aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly referred to as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of legislation. 18.

NUMBER 7 OF 2024

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and innate characteristics without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, and environments located in the industrial sector.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic designation that can be used by various institutions providing services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. which specifically have the principal duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts for the protection of women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

(2) Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include the organization of handling issues related to the protection of women in the Region.

CHAPTER III

EFFORTS FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 24

In the effort to protect women victims of violence, the Regional Government shall be obligated to:

a. ensure the implementation of the fulfillment of women's rights and the provision of guarantees of security from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the region;
b. establish policies, programs, women's protection activities and guarantees for victim handling to eliminate all forms of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the region; and
c. provide guidance and supervision in the efforts to protect women carried out by the Regional Apparatus that handles governmental affairs in the field of Protection and Empowerment of Women.

Article 22

(1) The fulfillment of special needs of women relates to the protection of women from anything that may threaten the safety and/or health of women's reproductive organs.

Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Surakarta City. 2. Mayor is the Mayor of Surakarta. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Apparatus is the supporting element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region; 5. Woman is a person who is female from infancy, adolescence, adulthood to the elderly, who is recognized by law. 6. Protection is all efforts to fulfill rights and provide assistance to provide a sense of security to witnesses and/or victims that must be carried out by institutions in accordance with legislation. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties aimed at protecting women from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination as well as providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights. 8. Empowerment of Women is an effort to gain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept and be free from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion, directly or indirectly, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, both individual and collective, in the fields of politics, economics, law, education, social, culture and other aspects of life. 10. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ exploitation, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to gain both material and immaterial benefits. 11. Violence is any act that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstruction of the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 12. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually and psychologically including certain acts of arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 13. Online Gender-Based Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as KBGO, is violence that occurs through digital media or online platforms targeting women, including: comments or messages that are insulting, degrading, or belittling of Women, messages or comments threatening to commit physical or sexual violence against Women, disseminating victims' personal information (such as addresses, telephone numbers, or other identities) without permission with the aim of intimidating or harming victims, extortion involving threats to spread intimate images or videos of victims unless the victim meets the perpetrator's demands, spreading private photos or videos of an intimate nature without the consent of the woman in the content, use of technology to stalk or monitor victims continuously, often with the aim of frightening or controlling the victim, and digitally altering images or videos of women for the purpose of insulting, humiliating, or sexually exploiting. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, contraceptive coercion, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of human trafficking aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly referred to as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of legislation. 18.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and innate characteristics without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, and environments located in the industrial sector.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic designation that can be used by various institutions providing services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. which specifically have the principal duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts for the protection of women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and innate characteristics without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, and environments located in the industrial sector.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic designation that can be used by various institutions providing services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. which specifically have the principal duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts for the protection of women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and residing in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 21. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent to a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, suffering or distress either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Recovery of Victims is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25. Integrated Service is the provision of integrated services, multi-aspects, cross-function and sector for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders suffered. 28. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is a technical operational implementation unit within the work unit that carries out government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, exploitation, discrimination, and other problems. 33. Temporary Shelter is a service function to provide or provide access to temporary protection places that prioritize security and safety, as well as clothing, food, and supporting facilities for beneficiary needs. 34. Standard Operating Procedures, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Surakarta City. 2. Mayor is the Mayor of Surakarta. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Woman is a person who is female from infancy, adolescence, adulthood to the elderly, who is recognized by law. 6. Protection is all efforts to fulfill rights and provide assistance to provide a sense of security to witnesses and/or victims that must be carried out by institutions in accordance with legislation. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties aimed at protecting women from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination as well as providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights. 8. Empowerment of Women is an effort to gain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept and be free from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion, directly or indirectly, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, both individual and collective, in the fields of politics, economics, law, education, social, culture and other aspects of life. 10. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ exploitation, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to gain both material and immaterial benefits. 11. Violence is any act that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstruction of the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 12. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually and psychologically including certain acts of arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 13. Online Gender-Based Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as KBGO, is violence that occurs through digital media or online platforms targeting women, including: comments or messages that are insulting, degrading, or belittling of Women, messages or comments threatening to commit physical or sexual violence against Women, disseminating victims' personal information (such as addresses, telephone numbers, or other identities) without permission with the aim of intimidating or harming victims, extortion involving threats to spread intimate images or videos of victims unless the victim meets the perpetrator's demands, spreading private photos or videos of an intimate nature without the consent of the woman in the content, use of technology to stalk or monitor victims continuously, often with the aim of frightening or controlling the victim, and digitally altering images or videos of women for the purpose of insulting, humiliating, or sexually exploiting. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, contraceptive coercion, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of human trafficking aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly referred to as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of legislation. 18.

Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion, directly or indirectly, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, both individual and collective, in the fields of politics, economics, law, education, social, culture and other aspects of life. 10. Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Surakarta City. 2. Mayor is the Mayor of Surakarta. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Apparatus is the supporting element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region; 5. Woman is a person who is female from infancy, adolescence, adulthood to the elderly, who is recognized by law. 6. Protection is all efforts to fulfill rights and provide assistance to provide a sense of security to witnesses and/or victims that must be carried out by institutions in accordance with legislation. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties aimed at protecting women from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination as well as providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights. 8. Empowerment of Women is an effort to gain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept and be free from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion, directly or indirectly, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, both individual and collective, in the fields of politics, economics, law, education, social, culture and other aspects of life. 10. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ exploitation, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to gain both material and immaterial benefits. 11. Violence is any act that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstruction of the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 12. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually and psychologically including certain acts of arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 13. Online Gender-Based Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as KBGO, is violence that occurs through digital media or online platforms targeting women, including: comments or messages that are insulting, degrading, or belittling of Women, messages or comments threatening to commit physical or sexual violence against Women, disseminating victims' personal information (such as addresses, telephone numbers, or other identities) without permission with the aim of intimidating or harming victims, extortion involving threats to spread intimate images or videos of victims unless the victim meets the perpetrator's demands, spreading private photos or videos of an intimate nature without the consent of the woman in the content, use of technology to stalk or monitor victims continuously, often with the aim of frightening or controlling the victim, and digitally altering images or videos of women for the purpose of insulting, humiliating, or sexually exploiting. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, contraceptive coercion, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of human trafficking aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly referred to as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of legislation. 18.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and innate characteristics without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, and environments located in the industrial sector.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic designation that can be used by various institutions providing services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. which specifically have the principal duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts for the protection of women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 24

a. ensure the implementation of the fulfillment of women's rights and the provision of guarantees of security from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the region;

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and residing in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 21. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent to a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, suffering or distress either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Recovery of Victims is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25. Integrated Service is the provision of integrated services, multi-aspects, cross-function and sector for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders suffered. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is a technical operational implementation unit within the work unit that carries out government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, exploitation, discrimination, and other problems. 33. Temporary Shelter is a service function to provide or provide access to temporary protection places that prioritize security and safety, as well as clothing, food, and supporting facilities for beneficiary needs. 34. Standard Operating Procedures, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and innate characteristics without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, and environments located in the industrial sector.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic designation that can be used by various institutions providing services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. which specifically have the principal duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts for the protection of women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Article 10

Letter a Sufficiently clear Letter b Sufficiently clear Letter c Sufficiently Clear Letter d Sufficiently clear Letter e What is meant by inclusion is the implementation of women's protection carried out by inviting and involving everyone with various abilities, backgrounds, characteristics, status, conditions, ethnicity, culture and others and facilitating special needs based on such diversity and eliminating barriers that can prevent the equality of every woman in obtaining her rights.

Letter g What is meant by victim-based decision is decision-making on services provided must be based on confirmation with the victim.

Letter h Sufficiently clear Letter i Sufficiently clear Letter j What is meant by integration is services for women victims carried out by various elements or components that mutually integrate or cooperate harmoniously and synergistically to achieve certain goals in accordance with the needs of the victim.

Article 2

Letter a What is meant by respect for human rights is respect for, upholding human rights inherent in citizens, as well as protecting dignity and honor as human beings.

Letter b What is meant by non-discrimination is protection for all women without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, belief, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, political choice, legal status and physical or mental condition. Special treatment or action toward vulnerable groups of women with the aim that they obtain equality of rights is not included as an act of discrimination.

Letter c What is meant by gender justice is fair treatment given to women and men. What is meant by gender equality is a condition and position that describes equal, harmonious and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d What is meant by benefit is the implementation of women's protection that provides benefits to women in the form of welfare, equality and justice, security and avoidance of all forms of violence, exploitation and discrimination.

Temporary Shelter is a service function to provide or provide access to temporary protection places that prioritize security and safety, as well as clothing, food, and supporting facilities for beneficiary needs. 34. Standard Operating Procedures, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
